question.prompt: Teams \(A\) and \(B\) are playing in a basketball league where each game results in a win for one team and a loss for the other team. Team \(A\) has won \(\tfrac23\) of its games and team \(B\) has won \(\tfrac58\) of its games. Also, team \(B\) has won \(7\) more games and lost \(7\) more games than team \(A.\) How many games has team \(A\) played?

solutions.title: Count the extra games
solutions.explanation:
The extra \(7\) wins and \(7\) losses mean that team \(B\) has played \(14\) more games than team \(A\).

Let \(g\) be the number of games team \(A\) has played. Its wins total \(\frac23g\), so team \(B\) has \(\frac23g+7\) wins in \(g+14\) games. Applying team \(B\)'s winning fraction gives
\[
\frac23g+7=\frac58(g+14).
\]
Multiplying by \(24\), we obtain
\[
16g+168=15g+210,
\]
so \(g=42\).

Team \(A\) has played \(\boxed{42}\) games, choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).

solutions.title: Compare wins with twice the losses
solutions.explanation:
Team \(A\)'s winning fraction \(2/3\) means that its wins are twice its losses. Comparing twice the losses with the wins therefore gives a useful quantity.

Let \(W\) and \(L\) be team \(A\)'s wins and losses, so \(W=2L\). For team \(B\), twice the losses minus the wins is
\[
2(L+7)-(W+7)=(2L-W)+7=7.
\]
But team \(B\) loses \(3/8\) of its games and wins \(5/8\), so this difference is
\[
2\cdot\frac38-\frac58=\frac18
\]
of its total games. Therefore team \(B\) has played \(8\cdot7=56\) games.

Team \(A\) has played \(14\) fewer games, giving \(56-14=\boxed{42}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
